Over time, these improvements are expected to contribute to more equitable, sustainable and effective delivery of priority health services for the Nigerian population.
purposes.i|P017175001: This project aims to create diversified, sustainable and inclusive trade, business and economic opportunities for people in Central America and the Andean region, including women and vulnerable populations. It does so by strengthening public institutions, improving trade, business, and investment policies and programs, and by fostering equitable access to economic opportunities. Project activities include: (1) designing and delivering an on-demand technical assistance deployment platform that quickly responds to emerging needs of stakeholders and engages them at every stage. These stages include defining technical assistance needs, determining the length and format of assignments, and selecting advisors, volunteers and consultants; and (2) delivering hands-on training, mentorships and knowledge exchange workshops by deploying Canadian expert advisors and volunteers, and local experts.
purposes.i|P017182001: This project aims to support ongoing efforts to advance the participation of women in the nuclear security and non-proliferation field. The project seeks to engage at least 12 women from developing countries in the following activities: (1) providing funds for a gender equality event that engages other women in their home institutions; (2) providing a five-session webinar training series to develop knowledge and skills; and (3) conducting an in-person workshop to allow beneficiaries to engage in policy discussions with women experts from international institutions and participate in a tabletop exercise on nuclear risk.
purposes.i|P017191001: With Canada’s support, International Crisis Group is supporting conflict stakeholders take effective action to prevent, mitigate, manage or resolve the effects of crises and conflicts. Project activities include: (1) producing independent reports and briefings on Canada’s priority conflict situations and on global trends; (2) producing short, rapid response pieces on evolving conflict and crisis situations and global trends; (3) convening in-depth policy discussions with conflict stakeholders; (4) undertaking targeted engagement with relevant interlocutors and policy makers, including Canadian officials, to promote International Crisis Group analysis and recommendations, with a view to shape the debate and mobilize political support; and (5) promoting and disseminating International Crisis Group’s results and data widely, including through podcasts, citations in international and local media outlets, and via social media channels.
purposes.i|P017196001: This project aims to improve forensic science services in the State of Palestine so that courts and investigations can rely on accurate and trustworthy evidence. By strengthening laboratories, staff skills and systems, the project supports a justice system that is fair and works better for women, men and children. Project activities include: (1) upgrading forensic laboratories, equipment and databases to improve DNA, fingerprint, firearms and trace evidence analysis; (2) improving rules, procedures and quality control to ensure forensic work meets international standards; (3) training and mentoring forensic specialists across key disciplines; and (4) supporting police, prosecutors, judges and other justice actors to better understand and use forensic evidence and to work more effectively together.
purposes.i|P017197001: This project focuses on staffing key positions in the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) Secretariat in Haiti. CANADEM will draw on decades of experience in deploying experts to challenging contexts and will utilize its international roster of peace and security experts to rapidly recruit appropriate candidates. Project activities include: 1) advertising positions to recruit candidates, 2) conduct screening of candidates and submit a shortlist of candidates to the hiring panel conducting interviews; and 3) once selected, CANADEM will manage the contracting and deployment, including all financial, logistical, and duty of care elements throughout the assignment. This grant arrangement will enable funding for approximately 20 to 25 positions for up to two years.
purposes.i|P017198001: This project seeks to reduce the risks posed by small arms, light weapons, and ammunition to women, men, girls, and boys in Ukraine by strengthening the weapons and ammunition management (WAM) capacity of the National Police of Ukraine (NPU) and delivering community-level risk education. Project activities include the following: (1) conducting technical risk assessments of police armouries and surge storage sites in select locations, in line with international small arms control and ammunition management standards; (2) identifying gaps in NPU infrastructure, procedures, and capacity, including storage conditions, inventory systems, segregation practices, and personnel training; (3) constructing or refurbishing NPU weapons and ammunition storage facilities in line with international standards and sector best practices; (4) delivering targeted training to the NPU on the safe storage, handling, segregation, and inventory management of small arms, light weapons and ammunition; (5) integrating small arms and light weapons risk education into existing MAG explosive ordnance risk education programming; (6) delivering targeted small arms risk education, including Training of Trainers sessions for relevant national and local authorities, alongside mass media outreach and digital campaigns.
purposes.i|P017218001: November 2025 - Cyclone Ditwah made landfall in Sri Lanka, resulting in widespread flooding, landslides, and significant infrastructure damage across all 25 districts. Approximately 2.2 million people have been affected, with 635 confirmed fatalities and 370 individuals reported missing. With Global Affairs Canada’s support, WFP responds effectively to the humanitarian needs caused by Cyclone Ditwah by providing emergency food, nutrition, cash assistance and support to logistical operations. Project activities include: (1) providing food and nutrition assistance; (2) providing cash assistance; and (3) supporting logistical operations.
purposes.i|P017219001: This project aims to strengthen the ability of civil society organizations, independent media, human rights defenders, and vulnerable groups to operate safely in increasingly contested digital environments ahead of the 2026 elections in Colombia and Brazil. The project would strengthen digital resilience through improved capacity of civil society actors, journalists and human rights defenders to anticipate, mitigate, and recover from cyber threats, including denial-of-service attacks, censorship pressures, and online harassment. It would support the secure use of resilient digital platforms and communications tools to ensure continuity of operations for democratic actors during high-risk electoral periods. Particular attention would be given to the needs of women, gender-diverse individuals, and other vulnerable groups, who face disproportionate levels of online abuse and technology-facilitated intimidation.
purposes.i|P017229001: With Canada's support, the UN Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) enables national actors to manage conflicts more peacefully and foster just and inclusive societies by providing fast, flexible and catalytic funding to nationally owned, multi-dimensional and sectoral peacebuilding initiatives. Project activities include: (1) investing in cross-border and transition contexts, and in support of more inclusion of women and youth; (2) supporting national actors to strengthen, implement, or develop conflict prevention strategies; (3) providing liaison and advisory services and surge capacity to UN field teams to facilitate innovative collaboration with International Financial Institutions (IFIs) through the Partnership Facility; and (4) sharing knowledge from peacebuilders and partners at local and national level through the Impact Hub to enhance the ability of peacebuilders to make timely and evidence-informed decisions on peacebuilding programming and policy.
purposes.i|P017235001: This project aims to respond to the proliferation of small arms, light weapons and explosive ordnance in Central Sahel and Coastal West Africa. Working in five countries, the main activities of the project are to: (1) deliver explosive ordinance risk education sessions to people affected by armed violence in border regions; (2) provide weapons and ammunitions management training to build the capacity of security sector agencies; (3) support local authorities to implement best practices in the management of small arms and light weapons; and (4) provide technical and institutional support to National Commissions to collaborate regionally to collectively address risks related to small arms and light weapons.
purposes.i|P017245001: This project aims to increase the security and resilience of artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) communities in Colombia’s Chocó, Cauca and Caldas Departments through ensuring stronger women’s roles in peace and security. The project aims to achieve this by empowering women miners to organize, advocate, and lead interventions that reduce community vulnerability to conflict, violence, and insecurity. Project activities include: (1) assessing safety and security risks in artisanal mining, including gender impacts, and supporting communities to discuss solutions; (2) training women miners groups to prevent and respond to violence and conflict in their communities; (3) working with local governments to include measures that prevent violence against artisanal miners in community development plans; and (4) strengthening women miners' groups so they can track progress on commitments, share lessons learned, and work more effectively with local, regional, and national authorities.
purposes.i|P017261001: This project seeks to strengthen radiological security in the Indo-Pacific. It supports activities aimed at strengthening physical protection measures at facilities housing high-activity radiological material. Project activities include: (1) building a secure national storage facility for disused radioactive sources in Nepal; and (2) providing capacity building courses in building nuclear security culture to strengthen physical protection measures to Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and to the Pacific Region.
purposes.i|P017274001: This project aims to increase the economic participation and self reliance of marginalized young adults in Dominica by equipping them with marketable vocational, business, and life skills. By targeting high school dropouts, single parents, and youth with disabilities, groups heavily affected by past disasters and systemic exclusion, the project enables participants to secure employment, start small businesses, and build long term resilience. Project activities include: (1) delivering 6 months of vocational training in welding, auto mechanics, massage therapy, masonry, carpentry, electrical installation, food preparation, garment production, and hair care services across seven districts; (2) providing a dedicated second cycle of business and financial empowerment training to strengthen entrepreneurial capacity and support small business start up or expansion; (3) offering psychosocial support, mentorship, childcare support systems, and flexible, community based training schedules to improve learning retention and accessibility for participants with caregiving responsibilities or disabilities; and (4) coordinating outreach campaigns, transportation logistics, and training of facilitators to ensure accessible, standardized, and inclusive technical and vocational education and training (TVET) delivery.
purposes.i|P017275001: This project aims to strengthen the resilience of primary school children in a high-risk community in Grenada by improving their literacy, emotional regulation, and access to supportive school and home environments. The project seeks to reduce early risk factors linked to youth crime and promote a school culture of safety, belonging, and pro social behavior. Project activities include: (1) implementing a structured literacy support program, including baseline assessments, specialized assessments for learning disabilities, and teacher training in literacy interventions; (2) delivering a tailored social emotional learning (SEL) program featuring workshops for teachers, student activities, guest speakers, field trips, and community engagement with the Royal Grenada Police Force; (3) conducting 3 parenting workshop series on social emotional learning at home and positive discipline to strengthen family engagement and protective factors; and (4) producing a knowledge product summarizing research findings, lessons learned, and tools for replicating SEL and literacy interventions in other primary schools.
purposes.i|P017276001: This project aims to increase the employability and socio economic well being of young people in Grenada by equipping them with industry recognized skills and practical experience in the hospitality sector. Through competency based training and structured apprenticeships, the project supports a more professional, inclusive, and environmentally responsible hospitality workforce capable of meeting labour market needs in Grenada’s tourism industry. Project activities include: (1) implementing a replicable hospitality apprenticeship model through partnerships with hotels, combining classroom instruction with on the job training and mentorship; (2) delivering competency based training to 40 apprentices (15 pastry chef trainees, 10 bartending trainees, and 15 housekeeping supervisor trainees) leading to Caribbean Vocational Qualification (CVQ) certification; (3) strengthening inclusive access to technical and vocational education and training (TVET) by proactively recruiting women, unemployed/underemployed youth, and youth from underserved or rural communities, while providing targeted support services; and (4) conducting gender sensitivity, workplace inclusion, and environmental sustainability sessions, as well as public awareness campaigns to promote equitable access to TVET.
purposes.i|P017277001: This project aims to create a safer, more inclusive Saint Lucia by empowering young people who are blind, visually impaired, or face additional barriers with the skills, confidence, and independence needed to participate fully in school, work, and community life. By reducing social exclusion and vulnerability, key risk factors for exploitation, abuse, and unsafe environments, the project strengthens crime prevention systems and enhances long term social protection for at risk youth. Project activities include: (1) providing life skills, digital literacy, orientation and mobility training, and daily living skills to 30 youth aged 13 to 35 who are blind, visually impaired, or living with other barriers; (2) engaging 5 employers through awareness sessions, accessibility assessments, and job shadowing placements to promote inclusive hiring and safe workplace environments; (3) procuring and installing assistive technology, such as braille embossers, screen readers, laptops, tablets, and accessibility software, to support participants’ digital access, communication, and learning; and (4) conducting outreach campaigns using schools, youth centers, communities, radio, and social media to reduce stigma, encourage safe participation, and strengthen awareness of disability inclusion.
purposes.i|P017278001: Youth unemployment in Saint Lucia remains a major challenge, especially for underserved communities with limited access to skills training and certification. This project aims to provide a competency-based apprenticeship program for 30 unemployed youth ages 18 to 29, combining classroom instruction with hands-on training through partnerships with 12 bakery operations, the Bakers Association, and the Ministry of Commerce. Over 12 months, participants will pursue Caribbean Vocational Qualification/National Vocational Qualification (CVQ/NVQ) certification at Levels 1 and 2, improving employability and helping meet workforce needs in the baking sector. The project promotes inclusion by encouraging at least 20% enrolment from the Offenders’ Reintegration Project and supporting gender equity. A public awareness campaign will help shift negative perceptions of the baking industry and increase interest in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) opportunities. Ultimately, the project aims to expand the pool of work-ready, certified professionals and strengthen socio-economic prospects for youth across key communities in Saint Lucia.
purposes.i|P017279001: This project aims to improve the employability, digital readiness, and economic empowerment of Vincentians by equipping 150 participants with practical Information and Communication Technology (ICT), financial literacy, entrepreneurship, and cybersecurity skills. By increasing access to accredited digital training and targeted mentorship, the project contributes to a more resilient, inclusive, and future ready workforce in St. Vincent and the Grenadines. Project activities include: (1) providing competency based ICT training, including CompTIA, Microsoft Office Suite, Google tools, and introductory artificial intelligence (AI) applications, to strengthen digital literacy and workplace productivity; (2) delivering financial literacy and financial management workshops, including accredited QuickBooks training and entrepreneurship mentoring to support business development; (3) training participants in cybersecurity through practical workshops developed with specialized partners; and (4) offering blended (online and in person) accredited courses to ensure flexible access for diverse genders, abilities, and age groups.
purposes.i|P017280001: This project aims to improve the well being and resilience of families in Suriname by increasing access to high quality, professional family counselling services. The project seeks to help ensure that families experiencing stress, conflict, or psychological challenges receive timely, effective support by training a cohort of counsellors in evidence based methods. Project activities include: (1) developing and validating a comprehensive, evidence based training curriculum and practical case studies for family counselling; (2) delivering training to 20 participants through interactive lectures, hands on practice, supervision sessions, and continuous feedback; and (3) establishing and supporting a local professional network of trained counsellors to facilitate collaboration, referrals, and ongoing knowledge exchange.
purposes.i|P017281001: This project aims to strengthen Suriname’s construction sector by increasing the number of skilled, certified workers who can meet modern industry and green infrastructure standards. By equipping apprentices with updated technical, environmental, and safety skills, the project contributes to a more competitive, professional, and sustainable construction workforce that can support national development. Project activities include: (1) developing and finalizing a competency based curriculum in sustainable green construction, supported by qualified trainers and appropriate training facilities; (2) delivering 8–9 weeks of combined classroom and hands on practical training, including technical, environmental, and health and safety modules; (3) recruiting and selecting 50 apprentices, prioritizing unemployed youth and underemployed workers, and placing them in on the job apprenticeships with certified construction firms; and (4) establishing formal partnerships with construction companies and contractors to provide mentorship, job placements, and career progression opportunities.
purposes.i|P017282001: This project aims to reduce explosive threats to civilians in southern and eastern Lebanon through the survey and clearance of unexploded ordnance focusing on heavily affected agricultural and residential zones, using mechanical assets to access complex terrain and remove rubble. MAG will rehabilitate infrastructure and provide equipment to enable safe storage for weapons and ammunition, in close coordination with the Lebanese Mine Action Center, Lebanese civil society and LAF, to ensure civilian safety, reduce immediate threats, support safe return, and stabilization. Project activities include: (1) Deployment of three mine action teams (MATs) to conduct technical survey (TS), clearance, and disposal spot tasks across priority contaminated areas; (2) Deployment of two CL teams and one mechanical team to conduct non-technical survey (NTS) and deliver explosive ordnance risk education (EORE); (3) Construct one explosive storehouse (ESH) to expand safe ammunition storage capacity; (4) Procurement and donation of specialized equipment, including a heavy-duty forklift and X-ray inspection machine, to enhance safe handling and inspection of munitions; (5) Implementation of priority WAM upgrades, including rehabilitation of storage infrastructure at selected sites.
purposes.i|P017283001: This project aims to protect civilians and support early recovery in northern and central Syria by enabling safe access to land, infrastructure, and essential services through the reduction of risks posed by landmines and other explosive ordnance. Project activities include: (1) conducting technical surveys, manual clearance, and explosive ordnance disposal to identify, remove, and destroy explosive hazards in prioritized areas; (2) deploying mechanical assets to support safe and efficient land release for agricultural, community, and infrastructure use; (3) delivering explosive ordnance risk education sessions to help women, men, girls, and boys recognize risks and adopt safer practices; (4) training community members as focal points to report contamination and share safety information within their communities; and (5) strengthening the technical and coordination capacity of national authorities and partner organizations to manage mine action activities in line with international standards.
purposes.i|P017289001: This project supports the Joint Programme of the United Nations Development Programme and United Nations Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, which deploys Peace and Development Advisors. These advisors help United Nations (UN) agencies, national authorities and other peace and conflict stakeholders prevent and resolve conflict and build peace. Project activities include: (1) developing or improving national, regional or sub-regional prevention strategies, plans and institutions for peace; (2) enhancing opportunities for women and youth to engage in and influence conflict prevention and peacebuilding efforts; (3) providing analytical and advisory services, and developing programming, for UN agencies and engagement; and (4) facilitating collaboration and coherence among UN entities and global partnerships with peace and conflict stakeholders, including with international financial institutions.
purposes.i|P017291001: This project aims to support the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), the International Organization for Migration’s (IOM) primary data collection program. The DTM helps track and monitor displacement and population mobility, provide critical information to decision-makers and responders during humanitarian crises, and deepen understanding of population flows around the world. The project seeks to target various countries where DTM needs are most critical and where funding can have the greatest impact. This includes Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Myanmar, South Sudan, Ukraine, and Yemen. With GAC’s support, the IOMs DTM strengthens its capacity for comprehensive data collection and in-depth analysis on displacement. It does so by generating timely, reliable, and actionable information for decision-makers, enhancing the effectiveness of humanitarian planning and response. This project aims to contribute to saving lives, reducing suffering, and safeguarding human dignity in countries affected by crises by improving evidence-based prioritization of resources, particularly for donors.
purposes.i|P017292001: This project aims to strengthen locally-led efforts to protect vulnerable youth from recruitment into armed groups in the Colombian border departments of Arauca and Putumayo by promoting International Humanitarian Law (IHL). Project activities include: (1) tailored training for religious leaders on IHL and humanitarian negotiations; (2) establishing or reinforcing community protection committees consisting of communities and religious leaders; (3) implementing community-based activities for children at risk of recruitment by armed groups; (4) producing social media videos targeting children and adolescents that counter recruitment campaigns by armed groups; and (5) strengthening or establishing early-warning mechanisms and safe communication channels for at-risk communities.
purposes.i|P017293001: This project aims to strengthen the integrity of the Haitian National Police (HNP) by supporting the establishment of its Polygraph Unit. Project activities include: (1) training, mentoring and certification for existing and new HNP polygraph experts; (2) expansion of the physical office space and provision of equipment; and (3) support to management in strategic planning, operational strengthening and institutionalization.
purposes.i|P017296001: March 2026 - Sudan is facing one of the world’s most severe and complex humanitarian crises, driven by armed conflict, mass displacement, collapsing state institutions, and recurring disease outbreaks. The ongoing conflict has resulted in the largest internally displaced population globally and the collapse of livelihoods, markets, and services across the country. More than half the population are in need of humanitarian assistance. The impacts are felt across the region, heightening insecurity and driving large-scale refugee movements that are straining already fragile host countries. With GAC’s support, in a consortium led by Care Canada; Care, CLWR and Oxfam will respond to the emergency needs of people affected by the Sudan crisis in Sudan, Chad and South Sudan. Project activities include: (1) providing gender-responsive and inclusive protection services, including GBV prevention and response services; (2) providing safe drinking water; (3) rehabilitating gender-responsive and inclusive water systems, latrines and handwashing facilities; and (4) providing health care services, including sexual and reproductive health services.
purposes.i|P017298001: The International Committee of the Red Cross’ (ICRC) primary mission is to protect the lives and dignity of people affected by armed conflicts and other situations of violence. The ICRC assists and works to prevent further suffering by promoting and strengthening international humanitarian law. The ICRC collaborates with local Red Cross and Red Crescent national society staff and volunteers to implement its protection and assistance programmes worldwide. This project aims to provide protection, emergency relief, and other essential services to people affected by armed conflict and other situations of violence. This includes in Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Colombia, DRC, Ethiopia, Haiti, Lebanon, Mali, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nigeria, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Ukraine, Venezuela and Yemen. Project activities include: (1) engaging with warring parties on the respect for international humanitarian law; (2) conducting protection activities to support those protected under international humanitarian law (people deprived of liberty, missing and separated, civilian populations); (3) assisting people affected by conflict and violence by providing medical care, income support, and food assistance; (4) working and abiding by the fundamental principles such as neutrality, impartiality, and independence, with all stakeholders; and (5) negotiating safe access to populations in need.
purposes.i|P017298002: The International Committee of the Red Cross’ (ICRC) primary mission is to protect the lives and dignity of people affected by armed conflicts and other situations of violence. The ICRC assists and works to prevent further suffering by promoting and strengthening international humanitarian law. The ICRC collaborates with local Red Cross and Red Crescent national society staff and volunteers to implement its protection and assistance programmes worldwide. This project aims to provide protection, emergency relief, and other essential services to people affected by armed conflict and other situations of violence. This includes in Palestine. Project activities include: (1) engaging with warring parties on the respect for international humanitarian law; (2) conducting protection activities to support those protected under international humanitarian law (people deprived of liberty, missing and separated, civilian populations); (3) assisting people affected by conflict and violence by providing medical care, income support, and food assistance; (4) working and abiding by the fundamental principles such as neutrality, impartiality, and independence, with all stakeholders; and (5) negotiating safe access to populations in need.
purposes.i|P017299001: The IOM Global Appeal 2026 (EDRMS 12169334) sets out a prioritized, people-centred response to address rising humanitarian needs, displacement and unsafe migration worldwide. Aligned with IOM’s Strategic Plan 2024–2028 (EDRMS 12169347), the Appeal seeks to support 41 million people on the move and in host communities, while strengthening systems that enable safe, orderly and regular migration. In a context of conflict, climate shocks and protracted crises, IOM positions migration as part of the solution, delivering immediate assistance while building long-term resilience. The Global Appeal is structured around three strategic objectives: 1. Saving lives and protecting people on the move: IOM delivers life-saving humanitarian assistance and protection services to migrants and displaced populations, reducing risks along migration routes and ensuring access to essential services in crisis contexts. 2. Driving solutions to displacement: IOM advances durable, sustainable solutions by supporting resilience, addressing climate-related mobility, and enabling voluntary, safe and dignified return and sustainable reintegration, in partnership with governments and communities. 3. Facilitating pathways for regular migration: IOM expands safe and regular migration pathways by strengthening migration governance, labour mobility schemes and rights-based policies that reduce reliance on dangerous irregular journeys. Across all objectives, the Appeal emphasizes flexible funding, stronger data and coordination, and a route-based approach to deliver timely, efficient and accountable responses, while advancing the commitments of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration
purposes.i|P017301002: February 2026 – The magnitude and severity of death, destruction and extreme deprivation in the Gaza Strip have generated profound human suffering and humanitarian needs. In the West Bank, demolitions, operations by Israeli forces, settler violence, and movement restrictions continue to trigger displacement and drive a range of humanitarian needs. The erosion of community resilience mechanisms has further intensified needs across all sectors. The United Nations estimates that 3.62 million people require lifesaving assistance across Palestine. With GAC’s support, the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) contributes to stabilizing conditions, restoring and scaling up the delivery of essential services, protecting the most vulnerable and providing life-saving humanitarian assistance to those in need. Project activities include providing emergency assistance, including food, healthcare, water and protection services to meet the basic needs of Palestinians.
purposes.i|P017302001: February 2026 - Food insecurity remains at alarming level in many countries, driven by conflicts, climate change, and economic shocks. The World Food Programme (WFP) is the United Nations’ frontline agency in the fight against hunger. It responds to emergencies and saves lives by quickly getting food assistance to crisis-affected populations. WFP also provides common services to humanitarian agencies by transporting humanitarian workers and light cargo and conducting emergency medical and security evacuations. With the support of Global Affairs Canada (GAC), WFP provides targeted emergency food assistance to crisis-affected populations to reduce acute food insecurity and malnutrition and protect livelihoods. Project activities include: (1) distributing food and cash-based transfers; (2) providing supplementary feeding for children under the age of 5 years, as well as pregnant and lactating women and girls; and (3) providing logistical support to humanitarian agencies and enabling access to the most remote and hard-to-reach locations. This project operates in multiple countries, including Bangladesh, Cameroon, Central Africa Republic, Chad, Colombia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Mali, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nicaragua, Nigeria, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Uganda, Ukraine, Venezuela, Yemen and Globally.
purposes.i|P017308001: This project seeks to strengthen radiological security in Cambodia. It supports activities aimed at strengthening the capacity of law enforcement to detect the illicit trafficking of radioactive material. Project activities include: (1) providing radiation detection equipment to the National Authority for the Prohibition of Chemical, Nuclear, Biological and Radiological Weapons of the Kingdom of Cambodia (NACW); (2) delivering a training on equipment operation, standard operating procedures on interdictions, and related field drills; (3) supporting the development of standard operating procedures for the effective use and deployment of the equipment; and (4) implementing a series of scenario-based field exercises to test readiness and identify gaps in training, organizational response, and procedures.
purposes.i|P017311001: Lighthouse, the Global Protection Fund, is a multi-donor pooled fund to establish a dynamic sub-granting platform that advances the protection of Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) by channelling resources directly to those at risk, supporting localization, fostering flexibility, and enabling at-risk HRDs and civil society organizations (CSOs) to sustain their work where needs and impact are greatest. The ultimate goal of Lighthouse is that HRDs, civil society groups, and movements most at risk worldwide are safer, more resilient, and better able to continue their human rights work through strengthened, coordinated, and needs-driven global protection efforts. Project activities include: (1) processing grant applications, including verification of identity and human rights work; (2) accompanying the recipient to ensure that measures are effective and that risks and threats are handled adequately; (3) collecting accurate and useful data across programs on threats faced by HRDs; and (4) disseminating the report with key stakeholders within the protection ecosystem, such as the United Nations, European Union, and national governments.
purposes.i|P017340001: This project aims to ensure that vulnerable youth in San Ignacio and Santa Elena can participate fully in Belize’s economy by removing the barriers that prevent them from accessing education, vocational training, and formal employment. With legal identity documents and practical job skills, these young people—especially those at risk of marginalization—will have greater opportunities for safe, stable, and sustainable livelihoods. To achieve this long-term change, the project carries out several concrete activities drawn from the logic model and activity list, including: 1) community outreach and registration, conducted with schools, civil society, and local organizations to identify undocumented youth and raise awareness about the importance of legal identity; 2) mobile documentation clinics, operated in partnership with government agencies, to help up to 150 youth obtain birth certificates, Social Security cards, and other required IDs; 3) vocational skills training, delivered with St. Ignatius High School, including technical trades (such as welding, hospitality, and entrepreneurship), paired with life skills and financial literacy modules; 4) paid apprenticeships and mentorships with local businesses (e.g., Westrac Ltd, Cahal Pech Resort, St. Martin’s Credit Union), providing real-world work experience supported by industry mentors; and 5) post-training job placement support, including interview preparation, job readiness coaching, and three months of follow-up to help graduates secure employment.
purposes.i|P017341001: This project aims to ensure that at-risk youth in Southern Belize can build safer, more resilient, and more productive futures by strengthening their cultural identity, leadership skills, and economic opportunities. Through arts-based empowerment, civic engagement, and practical livelihood training, the project seeks to reduce youth vulnerability to crime while equipping them with the confidence, skills, and resources needed to pursue meaningful employment or entrepreneurship. To achieve this long-term change, the project implements several concrete activities, including: (1) cultural and artistic engagement, such as the youth-led Lens on Heritage documentation initiative, intergenerational cultural exchanges, and community cultural showcases that strengthen identity and pro-social behaviour; (2) leadership development, delivered through Youth Leadership Circles, “Real Talk” peer dialogue podcast sessions, and youth-led community initiatives that build civic responsibility and emotional resilience; (3) entrepreneurship and livelihood training, including an 8-week business bootcamp, mentorship, seed funding, and the creation of 8–12 micro-enterprise clusters supported by shared Micro-Enterprise Kits; (4) accredited technical training, enrolling youth in Level 1 Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programs (e.g., electrical installation, carpentry, garment construction, Information and Communication Technology (ICT), agro-processing) to build marketable, job-ready skills; and (5) operation of a Community Hub, offering free Wi-Fi, printing services, cultural activities, business support sessions, and ongoing access to youth-friendly services through partnerships with local institutions.
purposes.i|P017342001: This project aims to ensure that young apprentices in Orange Walk and Belize Districts gain fair access to well-paid, sustainable careers in technical trades, particularly in Air Conditioning (AC), Refrigeration, and Electrical Installation. By receiving industry-recognized training and certification, including environmentally responsible practices, youth will be better equipped to secure employment, start their own businesses, and contribute to a more climate-resilient and skilled national workforce. To achieve this long-term change, the project implements several concrete activities, including: 1) developing and delivering an inclusive apprenticeship curriculum, aligned with Regional Occupational Standards and integrating environmental responsibility, sustainable technologies, and safe handling of refrigerants; 2) establishing partnerships with at least 5 AC, Refrigeration, and Electrical businesses, formalized through memoranda of understanding (MOUs) that secure workplace training, supervision, and adherence to safety protocols; 3) providing hands-on technical training, combining theory, practical workshops, workplace simulations, and ethics and safety modules to prepare 20 apprentices for real industry environments; 4) strengthening certification capacity, including training instructors and industry personnel to develop assessment instruments and gather evidence required for Caribbean Vocational Qualification (CVQ) Level 2 certification; 5) monitoring apprenticeship progress and preparing CVQ Level 2 portfolios, ensuring that all apprentices meet competency standards and have complete submissions for certification through the approved National Training Agency.
purposes.i|P017376001: This joint initiative by the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Women (UN Women), and the International Organization for Migration (IOM) under the UN Action Network, aims to strengthen a multisectoral, coordinated, and survivor-centred response to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) that has proliferated due to gang violence in Haiti. Project activities include: (1) improve emergency medical care for survivors of sexual violence; (2) provide specialized, conflict-sensitive mental health and psychosocial support; (3) offer legal support, guidance, and protection, including safe relocation when needed, for survivors seeking justice; (4) support survivors' recovery and reintegration through grants, mentoring, and livelihood opportunities; and (5) facilitate coordination, information sharing, and data management among participating UN organizations and the Gang Suppresion Force (GSF) to ensure safer, survivor-centered responses to sexual violence and other protection concerns.
purposes.i|P017389001: The aim of the project is to provide the Office of the Special Representative of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) with the resources required to implement the mandate given to the GSF by the United Nations Security Council (Resolution 2793 (2025). This project will provide the Special Representative, and by extension the GSF, with the resources for administrative and operational activities. Project activities include: 1) Hosting official meetings; 2) Developing a network of community stakeholders to build stability and peace alongside the GSF; 3) Implementation of quick impact projects; 4) Coordination of a strategic information operation strategy; and 5) Purchasing insurance against third-party claims.
purposes.i|P017404001: This project aims to strengthen the capacity of selected coastal local government units in the Philippines to anticipate, manage, and respond to complex maritime-related disruptions that affect community safety, essential services, and local governance. It shifts local planning from a hazard-specific approach toward an integrated, systems-based resilience model that strengthens civilian governance and protects communities during periods of uncertainty. This project seeks to support local authorities to plan for and manage the consequences of maritime disruptions in inclusive and risk-informed ways. It works through existing disaster risk reduction, crisis management, and governance structures to improve coordination, decision-making, and continuity of essential services. Project activities include: (1) strengthening the capacity of local government officials to identify and plan for maritime-related risks; (2) establishing localized and inclusive contingency plans to support the continuity of food supply, energy access, and communications; and (3) facilitating coordination and information-sharing between local and national institutions.
purposes.i|P017519001: This grant represents Canada's long-term institutional support to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA uses these funds and other donors' funding to achieve its mandate. OCHA's primary mandate is to coordinate international humanitarian responses in partnership with national and international actors to achieve more coherent and effective humanitarian action. With the support of Canada and other donors, OCHA fulfills its mandate by: (1) coordinating the global emergency response; (2) raising awareness of forgotten crises, promoting respect for international humanitarian law, bringing the voices of affected people to the forefront and helping people access assistance; (3) mobilizing and engaging the full range of financing instruments, mechanisms and partners to meet the growing needs; (4) developing policy to improve humanitarian action and decision-making; and (5) providing information management services to the humanitarian community to inform rapid, effective and principled responses.
purposes.i|P017540001: April 2026 – Lebanon is experiencing a sharp surge in humanitarian needs following the latest escalation of hostilities, which has driven large-scale displacement and intensified pressure on already fragile health and social support systems. The Lebanon Flash Appeal estimates 1.3 million people will be directly affected during the March–May 2026 response period, while WHO reports over 1 million self-registered internally displaced persons (IDPs), including many living in collective shelters. Intensified operations since early March have caused significant casualties and damage, including attacks affecting health workers, emergency medical services, and essential infrastructure, further threatening the continuity of life-saving and essential health services. With GAC’s support, Oxfam-Québec will 1) increase equitable access to safe, appropriate, and gender-responsive WASH services and supplies for IDPs, and 2) reduce protection risk rates among conflict-affected people.
purposes.i|P017541001: April 2026 – Lebanon is experiencing a sharp surge in humanitarian needs following the latest escalation of hostilities, which has driven large-scale displacement and intensified pressure on already fragile health and social support systems. The Lebanon Flash Appeal estimates 1.3 million people will be directly affected during the March–May 2026 response period, while WHO reports over 1 million self-registered internally displaced persons (IDPs), including many living in collective shelters. Intensified operations since early March have caused significant casualties and damage, including attacks affecting health workers, emergency medical services, and essential infrastructure, further threatening the continuity of life-saving and essential health services. With GAC’s support, World Vision Canada will 1) improve the use of immediate life-saving primary healthcare services for conflict-affected and displaced populations and vulnerable host communities, and 2) increase the immediate use of an enhanced protective environment and systems?to respond to protection issues.
purposes.i|P017542001: The escalation of hostilities between Hezbollah and Israel in early March 2026 is deepening the existing humanitarian and socio-economic crisis, with the health system particularly impacted. In response, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) revised its Emergency Appeal to reach up to 1.2 million people with critical services, including emergency medical care, food, shelter, and clean water, until December 2027. With $4 million in Global Affairs Canada’s support, the Canadian Red Cross is supporting the efforts of the Lebanese Red Cross to deliver life-saving humanitarian assistance as outlined in the revised IFRC Emergency Appeal for Lebanon. Project activities include: (1) delivering emergency medical services, including ambulance services, medical evacuations, and trauma stabilization; (2) operating hospitals, field hospitals, medical points, clinics, and mobile medical units; (3) providing mental health and psychosocial support services; and (4) distributing emergency relief supplies, including food, water, hygiene items, and shelter assistance.
purposes.i|P017544001: The humanitarian situation in Lebanon deteriorated significantly following the sharp intensification of hostilities in early March 2026, which marked the most serious escalation since the November 2024 ceasefire. This escalation triggered renewed mass displacement, damaged critical civilian infrastructure, and further compounded an already severe humanitarian crisis. The United Nations estimates that up to 1 million people in Lebanon require urgent life-saving assistance over a three-month period. The Lebanon Humanitarian Fund, managed by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is an existing Country-Based Pooled Fund (CBPF) that mobilizes multi-sector emergency response allocations based on partner presence and capacity. With GAC’s support, the fund releases emergency funding for priority life-saving interventions, including protection, food security, health, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and shelter, with a strong focus on reaching the most vulnerable populations and enabling rapid scale-up by frontline responders. Project activities include: (1) providing needs-based assistance in line with priorities in the emergency Flash Appeal for Lebanon; (2) increasing operational response capacity and coverage through diverse partnerships with non-governmental organizations, including national and local actors; and (3) improving the timeliness, effectiveness, and efficiency of life-saving interventions through coordinated, flexible, and rapid allocation mechanisms.
purposes.i|P017545001: The World Food Programme (WFP) is the United Nations’ frontline agency in the fight against hunger. It responds to emergencies, saves lives by quickly getting food assistance (cash or in-kind) to vulnerable food insecure populations and helps prevent hunger. As the global lead agency for logistics and emergency telecommunications, WFP plays a major role in providing common services for the humanitarian community. It transports humanitarian workers, carries light cargo for humanitarian agencies and carries out emergency medical and security evacuations. This project operates in Lebanon. With the support of Global Affairs Canada (GAC), WFP provides targeted food assistance to vulnerable populations to reduce acute malnutrition and food insecurity and protect livelihoods. Project activities include: (1) distributing food and cash-based transfer; (2) providing supplementary feeding for children under the age of 5 years, as well as pregnant and lactating women; and (3) providing logistical support and enabling access to the most remote and challenging locations.
purposes.i|P017615001: The project aims to enhance the capabilities and resilience of Jordan's national authorities to prepare for, prevent and respond to chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) threats through: (1) the delivery of CBRN-related trainings; and (2) the delivery of technical exercises.
purposes.i|P017667001: June 2026 - A rapidly growing Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda has prompted the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare it a public health emergency of international concern. The WHO Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE) is a replenishable multi-donor fund that provides resources necessary to rapidly scale up the WHO’s initial response to health-related outbreaks and emergencies. With GAC’s support, the CFE helps the WHO react early to prevent health emergencies from escalating. Project activities include: (1) deploying experts to assess outbreak threat; (2) delivering essential medicines, supplies and equipment; (3) training health personnel; and (4) strengthening health sector coordination and health information systems.
purposes.i|P017941001: June 2026 - Two powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, causing widespread devastation across Caracas, La Guaira, and surrounding states. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, extensive damage to homes, critical infrastructure, and essential services, while displacing thousands of people. With support from Global Affairs Canada, the World Food Programme (WFP) is responding to the humanitarian needs arising from the earthquakes by providing emergency food assistance and logistical support. Project activities include: (1) providing food and nutrition assistance; (2) facilitating the movement and delivery of relief supplies; and (3) supporting logistics operations.
purposes.i|P017942001: June 2026 - Two powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, causing widespread devastation across Caracas, La Guaira, and surrounding states. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, extensive damage to homes, critical infrastructure, and essential services, while displacing thousands of people. With funding from Global Affairs Canada, the International Rescue Committee will provide urgent health, protection, as well as water, sanitation and hygiene services to those affected by the earthquakes. Project activities include: (1) facilitating access to essential medical supplies and equipment for health facilities; (2) delivering primary health services; (3) providing protection services including psychosocial support; (4) strengthening community-based protection and referral systems; and (5) supporting water, sanitation and hygiene needs.
purposes.i|P017996001: June 2026 – Two powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, causing widespread devastation across Caracas, La Guaira, and surrounding states. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, extensive damage to homes, critical infrastructure, and public services, while displacing thousands of people. To respond to needs emerging from this disaster, the Secretary of State (International Development) announced that Canada would match donations made to the Canadian Red Cross Society (CRCS) for Venezuela. With GAC’s support, the CRCS, via the International Federation of the Red Cross (IFRC), is enabling the Venezuelan Red Cross to deliver a comprehensive life-saving response. Project activities include: (1) providing emergency shelter assistance; (2) providing multipurpose cash assistance and essential relief items; (3) providing health services, including first aid, triage, emergency medical services, mental health and psychosocial support, and reinforcement of affected health facilities; (4) providing water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services; and (5) providing protection services, including restoration of family links, case management, and assistance for families searching for missing relatives.
purposes.i|P018015001: The Caribbean Regional Logistics Hub and Centre for Excellence serves as a central location to strengthen the region’s ability to efficiently respond to humanitarian emergencies. The Hub, co-led by the World Food Programme, supports the prepositioning and deploying emergency relief supplies, including food and basic items, and logistics capabilities and expertise in the Caribbean for emergency responses. With Global Affairs Canada's support, the WFP supports emergency preparedness and relief operations in the Caribbean. The project aims to enable timely and efficient emergency responses from WFP and for other humanitarian partners. Project activities include: (1) pre-positioning, procuring, distributing and transporting essential food and non-food items for crisis-affected people in official development assistance-eligible countries in the Caribbean; and (2) providing logistics equipment and technical assistance to impacted countries and humanitarian partners.
purposes.i|P018045001: June 2026 – Two powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, causing widespread devastation across Caracas, La Guaira, and surrounding states. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, extensive damage to homes, critical infrastructure, and public services, while displacing thousands of people. To respond to the needs emerging from this disaster, the Secretary of State (International Development) announced that Canada would match donations made to the Humanitarian Coalition and its members for Venezuela. With GAC’s support, the Humanitarian Coalition and its members are undertaking comprehensive life-saving relief operations across the impacted areas. Project activities include: (1) providing essential food and non-food relief items; (2) providing emergency shelter assistance; (3) providing safe, water, sanitation and hygiene services; (4) providing protection services including gender-based violence prevention; as well as (5) providing health services and psychosocial support to families and children affected by the disaster.
purposes.i|P018459001: August 2026 - Catastrophic flash floods triggered by a glacial collapse struck northern Nepal, causing widespread loss of life and extensive damage to homes, critical infrastructure, and livelihoods across the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading. The disaster left affected communities with urgent humanitarian assistance needs. With support from Global Affairs Canada, the World Food Programme (WFP) is responding to the humanitarian needs arising from the flash floods by providing emergency food assistance and logistical support. Project activities include: (1) providing food and nutrition assistance; (2) facilitating the movement and delivery of relief supplies; and (3) supporting logistics operations.
purposes.i|P018460001: August 2026 - Catastrophic flash floods triggered by a glacial collapse struck northern Nepal, causing widespread loss of life and extensive damage to homes, critical infrastructure, and livelihoods across the districts of Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading. The disaster left affected communities with urgent humanitarian assistance needs. With GAC’s support, the Canadian Red Cross Society and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies are working to save lives and help reduce the suffering of people affected by the floods. Project activities include: (1) distributing of essential relief items including temporary shelter materials, household supplies and hygiene items; (2) providing cash and voucher assistance to displaced and affected households; (3) providing emergency health services including mental health support.

notes: Fiscal years run 1 April to 31 March. A record counts in the fiscal year of its date: contracts by original award date, grants by agreement start date, IATI by disbursement date. The current year is partial (see fy_through), and the latest quarter or two of contracts and grants are thin because departments publish them quarterly, a month or more after the quarter ends.

Contracts: 'country' is the vendor's country (country_of_vendor), i.e. where the supplier is based, not where the work is done; a U.S. firm supplying a Canadian base counts as United States. Value is the contract's current total value booked on its award date, so multi-year deals count in full in the year they were signed.

Grants and contributions: 'country' is the recipient's mailing address (recipient_country), not where the money is spent. UN agencies and international NGOs are mostly addressed in New York, Geneva, Rome, Vienna, Paris or London, so those cities' countries collect money spent elsewhere. Value is the agreement's current total (latest amendment), counted in the year of the original start date, as on the federal page.

Canadian organisations delivering aid abroad: Global Affairs grants and contributions to Canadian-addressed recipients (WUSC, Cowater, Alinea, Plan Canada and the like) and its development-assistance contracts with Canadian firms are included and placed in the country the project serves, not at the Canadian address (record element a = 1). A grant is placed by the recipient countries of the matching GAC IATI activity (project number in agreement_number) and split by its percentages; failing that, by the countries named in its title, description and expected results, split evenly when several are named; otherwise it is unplaced as 'Canadian organisation, country not stated'. Contracts are placed the same way from the GAC project number or country names in their description and comments. Aid is recognised by an IATI project number or an international-assistance program (development, humanitarian, bilateral, multilateral and partnership programming, peace and stabilization, weapon threat reduction, counter-terrorism capacity, youth internships, CFLI); trade programs (CanExport, CIIP) and academic relations are left out. Contracts count when they use the development-assistance and transfer-payment object codes (23xx). Canadian-addressed grants from other departments are not included.

IATI (Global Affairs Canada only): 'country' is the activity's recipient country as GAC reports it, the best measure of where aid goes. Money is actual disbursements in the year (a flow), not agreement totals (a commitment), so it is not comparable dollar for dollar with grants. Multi-country activities are split by GAC's recipient-country percentages; the share GAC assigns to a region rather than a country is listed as unplaced under the region's name. Other departments' aid (e.g. Finance, IRCC) is not in this file.

Do not add the sources together: GAC's aid appears both in the grants file (by agreement) and in IATI (by disbursement). In 2025-26, 845 of the 1032 GAC activities with disbursements ($3.2B of $3.8B) match a GAC agreement in the grants file by project number (any start date, any recipient address), and 145 of the 323 GAC grants in the grants source ($1.4B of $3.9B) are IATI activities; the rest are mostly multi-year institutional pledges (Global Fund, Gavi, IFAD, development banks) and assessed contributions to the UN, NATO, OECD and similar bodies, which GAC does not report at project level.

Keyword flags are whole-word matches on English text (French only when no English is given): W women/girls, M men/boys, G gender, L LGBTQ2+ terms. A flag means the words appear in the title, description, program name or expected results, not that the money is targeted at that group. Contract descriptions are standard category labels (e.g. 'Management consulting'), so contracts almost never carry a flag. P and S are GAC's own OECD gender-equality policy marker (principal objective / significant objective) and exist for IATI records only.

Military, housing and climate flags: D marks military or defence terms (armed forces, weapons, ammunition, NATO, peacekeeping, navy and the like) and every record of a defence department (National Defence, Communications Security Establishment), which is flagged military by department whatever its text; H marks housing and shelter (housing, houses, shelter, homelessness, emergency or temporary accommodation); E marks carbon, emissions and climate (carbon, decarbonisation, emissions, greenhouse gases, net zero, climate in any sense, methane). Like the other flags they mean the words appear, not that the money is for that purpose.
Gender Inequality Index: UNDP Human Development Report, 2023 values; rank 1 = most equal among the 172 countries with a value. Lower is more equal.
Grants to individuals with a foreign address (mostly NSERC, SSHRC and CIHR fellowships held abroad and Canadian athletes training abroad) are counted under that country but not named.
10 foreign contracts of $100M or more across these years, worth $9.4B; they are multi-year deals booked in full in the year they were awarded.
